title: Dismiss low-battery notification when charger is connected
head: 51ae2cfb4bd3
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: #9883 plus this PR can leave a low battery with no visible warning after an AC flap
leads.consequence: If #9883 lands too, the first low event sets notifiedLowBattery; plugging in triggers this PR's dismissal, while #9883 deliberately keeps the latch set at 8%. If AC disappears again before recovery, checkBattery sees notify=false, so the sticky warning remains dismissed even though the battery is critically low and discharging. It is not re-created at the next 30s poll. Coordinate dismissal and latch reset/realert across AC flaps so a removed warning is restored on unplug without reintroducing the repeated-toast storm #9883 prevents.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); corroboration; published within F2

leads.summary: #11161 plus this PR immediately retracts a warning from an underpowered charger
leads.consequence: #11161 intentionally warns when DisplayDevice is discharging below 10% despite onBattery=false with AC online (e.g. a low-wattage dock). The warning script finishes, emits warningProcess.exited, and this PR immediately dismisses its freshly sent toast because onBattery is false. No new warning is eligible until the latch clears, so the battery can run down without a persistent alert. Gate dismissal on actual recovery/charging, not AC presence alone, if these PRs coexist.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); corroboration; published within F2

leads.summary: The dismiss needle will not match #7434's localized battery warning
leads.consequence: #7434 translates the producer headline. In Spanish it sends '¡Es hora de recargar!', while this PR passes fixed English 'Time to recharge!' to a case-sensitive substring search. Even after an AC transition the Spanish critical popup stays visible and is restored on shell restart. Derive the matching summary from the same translation (or match by a stable nonlocalized identity/id) when integrating #7434.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified coord/pr-7434.diff (omarchy_t wraps title; PR dirty vs quattro); Opus self-check added locale qualifier; published as one sentence in Optional test improvement

leads.summary: #11415 and this PR both define dismissLowBatteryWarning(), with incompatible guards
leads.consequence: Applying #11415's own diff to this head succeeds but yields two definitions of dismissLowBatteryWarning() with the same signature. Its checkBattery() expects that method to launch dismissWarningProcess on battery recovery; the later definition from this PR instead does nothing when onBattery=true. If the other definition wins, this PR's onExited can launch dismissal even while battery is still low. Merge the helpers into one explicitly before integrating either PR; both AC arrival and recovery above the threshold need to dismiss without suppressing a new warning.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1) with stronger runtime evidence; corroboration

leads.summary: #12115 conflicts in the warningProcess callback and has a competing clear/retry protocol
leads.consequence: #12115 retains a clear-pending flag and retries dismissals until the warning is gone; its test depends on clearWarningProcess.onExited rechecking a deferred warning. Our onExited callback is added at the exact Process { id: warningProcess } block that its diff replaces. The three-way merge using the shared Service.qml base produces a conflict in that block, not a clean combined service. Resolving by keeping either hook alone loses the other's post-notification handling; if both are kept, coordinate parallel dismissals with its pending flag and tests.
leads.triage: factual; not in Opus final; coordinator verified coord/pr-12115.diff and sol/merged-base/12115-merged-Service.qml conflict markers; Opus confirmed by test merge in self-check; published in F1 table

leads.summary: An already-connected charger at shell start leaves a restored warning on screen
leads.consequence: After an update/restart or shell crash, a critical warning persisted from the previous session is restored asynchronously by NotificationService. If the shell starts with onBattery already false, this service never sends another warning (so warningProcess.onExited never fires), and no onBatteryChanged event is required to occur. Its only Component.onCompleted call refreshes the power profile; it does not dismiss. The critical toast can therefore remain indefinitely despite AC, until power toggles again or the user manually dismisses. Also -q makes IPC unavailability a silent success, so an early best-effort dismissal has no retry. Reconcile startup/restoration and retry after the notification service is ready.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F4); published as Not covered note with Opus's qualifier

leads.summary: Existing battery tests cannot catch a wrong or missing dismissal callback
leads.consequence: The only battery unit test loads BatteryModel.js, not Service.qml; removing the new onExited or onOnBatteryChanged call, or misspelling the summary, leaves all seven assertions green. Add a test that extracts/invokes the QML function or uses a controlled Quickshell fixture with UPower and execDetached stubs to assert charger and warning-exit behaviours, including the low→AC→low episode. This is a specific plausible mutant, not a request for a generic new test suite.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3); published as Optional test improvement

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** For an ordinary charger, the change does what the description says. Plugging in flips `UPower.onBattery` to false, and the shell runs `omarchy-notification-dismiss "Time to recharge!"`. That reaches the notifications service's `dismiss(summary)` handler, which removes every popup whose summary contains that text. This matters because critical toasts in this shell never expire on their own. The extra `warningProcess.onExited` call covers the case where the charger is connected before `omarchy-battery-low` has posted its toast: the first dismiss finds nothing, and the second runs after the toast has been added. The PR merges cleanly onto current `quattro`. The dismiss path there (the socket fast path in `omarchy-shell` and `ShellIpc` in the notifications service) still reaches the same, unchanged `dismiss(summary)` handler.

The two points below concern other open PRs and one hardware case, not the ordinary-charger path.

### Three other open PRs implement the same dismissal; one combination stops the battery service loading

#8036, #11415 and #12115 also dismiss the "Time to recharge!" toast, each in its own way. How they combine with this PR:

| Combined with | Git result | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #11415 | Textual merge is clean | `Service.qml` declares `function dismissLowBatteryWarning()` twice. `qmllint` reports `Duplicated method name`, and a minimal Qt runtime repro of a duplicate method fails to load with `Duplicate method name`. |
| #12115 | Conflict | Both change the `Process { id: warningProcess }` block. #12115 adds its own `clearWarningProcess` with a retry and recheck protocol. |
| #8036 | Conflict | Both edit `onOnBatteryChanged`. |

**Impact:** If this PR and #11415 both land, nothing flags the problem at merge time. The duplicate method stops `Service.qml` from loading, so the shell skips the battery service. Low-battery warnings and automatic AC/battery power-profile switching then stop. The headless `test/shell` suite reads `Service.qml` only as text, so it would not catch this.

**Suggested change:** Settle on one implementation among #8036, #11415, #12115 and this PR. If more than one lands, merge the helpers into a single function rather than keeping two definitions.

### "Not on battery" does not mean the battery stopped draining

The dismissal is keyed on `UPower.onBattery` alone. In upower 1.91.4 (`src/up-daemon.c`), `OnBattery` is false as soon as any line-power supply reports online, even when the battery itself is still discharging. Open issue #10939 shows this on real hardware: a dock that supplies less than the draw reports AC online and `OnBattery` false while the battery drains from 20% to 2%.

```text
dock that supplies less than the draw, battery at 8% and still discharging
  onBattery: true -> false
    before this PR: critical "Time to recharge!" toast stays on screen
    this PR:        toast dismissed; no new warning while docked (the warning gate requires onBattery)
```

**Impact:** On such a charger or dock, the only low-battery toast disappears exactly when the user believes the laptop is charging. Two open PRs aimed at related hardware cases (#11161 for this dock case, #9883 for AC-online flapping) make it worse when combined with this one (based on source reading of the combined code):
- With #11161 (warn even when line power is online), a warning sent while docked is dismissed as soon as `omarchy-battery-low` exits, because `warningProcess.onExited` then sees `onBattery` false.
- With #9883 (keep the low-battery latch across AC flaps), the first flap to AC dismisses the toast, and the latch then suppresses any new warning until the level recovers above the threshold.

#8036, #11415 and #12115 rest on the same `onBattery` premise, so this is a design question for the feature as a whole.

**Suggested change:** Dismiss only when the battery is actually no longer discharging, for example when the display device state is Charging, FullyCharged or PendingCharge, not on `UPower.onBattery` alone. Recheck on state changes or on the existing 30-second `checkBattery` tick.

**Optional test improvement:** `"Time to recharge!"` is now hard-coded in both `Service.qml` and `bin/omarchy-battery-low`. `test/shell.d/battery-test.sh` only loads `BatteryModel.js`, so removing either new call, or rewording the toast title, leaves every assertion passing. An assertion that the dismissed string matches the summary `bin/omarchy-battery-low` sends would catch a silent mismatch. Other shell tests already check `Service.qml` text this way (for example `powerprofiles-set-test.sh`). Open PR #7434 translates that summary with `omarchy_t`, so under a translated locale a fixed English needle would stop matching there too.

**Not covered: toast restored after a shell restart.** If the charger was connected while the shell was not running, a toast restored when the shell starts again is not dismissed. That case produces no `onBattery` transition and no warning exit, so the toast stays until the next power change or a manual dismiss.

---

**Test scope:** Mostly source review of the pinned head (51ae2cfb) and current `quattro` (3faafba2), plus Quickshell v0.3.1, upower 1.91.4 and Qt 6.11.2 sources. Isolated command runs covered the existing battery and power-profile shell tests on head, on head merged onto `quattro`, and on that merge plus #11415; `qmllint` on the merged `Service.qml`; and a minimal Qt duplicate-method load test. Combinations with #11161 and #9883 were assessed from source. No live desktop, notification daemon or hardware charger testing.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
